name: Toast, Inc.
business_model: Razor-and-blade: restaurant software subscription plus payments take rate

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Toast sells restaurant and retail operators a point-of-sale system plus the card payments, payroll and loans that run through it; about 189,000 locations, ARR $2.5B (+24%).

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: 9M 2026 revenue $5,519M: financial technology (payments, mostly pass-through) $4,512M, subscriptions $875M, hardware and services $132M; subscription plus fintech gross profit $1,735M of total $1,506M after a hardware/services loss.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Mostly small and mid-sized restaurants (10-K: a majority are SMBs, more fragile in downturns); no customer above 10% of revenue in 2023-2025; enterprise chains (Applebee's etc.) and retail growing from a small base.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: Effectively all revenue is US (no material revenue elsewhere in 2023-25); staff in Ireland and India; Canada all 10 provinces; no real currency exposure, but also no geographic spread yet.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Razor-and-blade: subscription fee plus a cut of each card payment. Payments cost of revenue $1,239M on $1,619M fintech revenue in Q3 2026, so net take about 0.61% of $61.8B volume, same as a year ago (about 0.61%). Most gross profit rides on restaurant sales volume.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Software-like costs: GAAP operating income $165M on $630M recurring gross profit (26% margin, from 17% a year ago); capex only $48M in 9M. Watch: inventory $244M vs $114M at year-end, and $148M paid for contract acquisition costs in 9M. Guidance raised in Q3: FY gross profit growth 26% (was 23-25%), adj. EBITDA $840-850M (was $805-825M).

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Inputs: card payment processors/sponsor banks (interchange passes through to merchants, Toast keeps its spread), hardware from contract manufacturers, some on a single source (displays); 10-K says no long-term agreements with all suppliers. Tags: tariffs and dollar hit hardware cost; inflation/consumer_spending_nominal move volume; rates drive cash interest income ($36M in 9M). Hardware is a small, loss-making line (cost $357M vs revenue about $132M incl. services in 9M) so pass-through matters little; the payments take rate has held at 0.61%. Single bank partner for Toast Capital loans.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: All-in-one restaurant stack with switching costs (hardware, menus, payroll, payments in one login) and data for lending; record 30,000 net adds in 2025. Doing differently now: AI agents (Toast IQ Grow and Team), Toast Fuel for convenience stores.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Diners see Toast terminals daily but are not the buyer; to operators it is a well-known brand. Vanishing would hurt restaurants a lot, consumers little. Sales and marketing $493M in 9M, 8.9% of revenue ($171M in Q3 vs $144M).

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Competes with Square, Fiserv's Clover, legacy POS and niche tools. Gaining: locations +21% to 189,000 with about 8,500 net adds in Q3 and a record 30,000 in 2025. No filing gives total market share; 'nothing found' on a clean share figure.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Enterprise, international and retail passed 10,000 live locations in mid-2025 (10-K proxy); Canada complete; fuel and convenience launched. Core US restaurant base is still being converted. Not yet priced as a separate story; international revenue is not yet material.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: No debt, $1,885M cash and securities. FCF about $606M over the last 12 months (estimate: FY25 operating cash $661M plus 9M change, less capex) but 9M FCF flat at $426M vs $430M. SBC about $214M last 12 months. Bought back $486M (19M shares) in 9M and added $500M authorization. Dual-class: Class B holds about 55% votes. CFO and President Gomez leaves Dec 31, 2026 (successor internal).

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Gaining relevance: ARR +24%, locations +21%. Risks: restaurant cycle (SMB), cheap competition (Clover, Square), founder-led but CFO transition, and one major legal challenge to sales practices.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: Clean on accounting: no 8-K Items 4.01/4.02, no NT filings, no CORRESP/UPLOAD letters in the filing list back to 2022. But FTC and 7 states sued on Oct 29, 2026 (FTC Act, ROSCA: sales and cancellation practices); damages unestimated, no accrual. Critical audit matter is the Toast Capital credit-loss reserve (credit loss expense $87M in 9M vs $66M).

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Boom +; overheat 0 (nominal sales inflation lifts volume, but food and labour costs squeeze SMB restaurants; cash earns interest); stagflation - (real traffic flat, loan losses); slowdown - (volume-linked, high-multiple). Rate sensitivity: higher rates add interest income, hurt loans; dollar negligible (US revenue).

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: FTC complaint filed Oct 29, 2026 seeking injunction, money relief and civil penalties (docket: N.D. Cal., 10-Q note); interchange rules and Credit Card Competition Act would change who keeps the payment spread; Toast offers surcharging.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Price $33.71 (close 2026-11-25), market cap $19.6B, EV about $17.7B (no debt, $1.9B cash). Reverse DCF at 10%/3%: needs about 12% yearly FCF growth for 10 years off $606M FCF, or about 18% if SBC ($214M) is counted as a cost (owner FCF $392M). Own record: FCF swung from negative in 2022 to about $606M, but 9M 2026 FCF is flat. Multiples: forward P/E 19.0, EV/FY26 adj. EBITDA guide about 21x vs Block 14.1 fwd P/E, PayPal 9.8, Fiserv 7.5. 5-year own multiple range: not retrieved (nothing found cheaply).

status_reason: Quality is B and growth and profit are real, but price needs about 12-18% yearly cash-flow growth for ten years, the FTC sued on Oct 29 and the CFO is leaving, and no clear market mistake shows.

feedback.fact: Restaurant POS payment volume (GPV) grew 20% to $61.8B in Q3 2026 with take rate steady at about 0.61%, so nominal restaurant spending was solid in Jul-Sep; October real spending flat is not yet in any company data.
feedback.reading: Supports Overheat in hard data (nominal volume up); does not yet confirm the Slowdown turn.
